title: Efficient Log-Scale Inventory Lookup
business: Warehouse management systems handling massive, sorted lists of serialized product IDs.
problem: Linear scanning through millions of sorted product records to find a specific insertion point or range causes significant latency during real-time inventory updates.
solution: Binary search (bisection) repeatedly halves the search interval by comparing the target value against the midpoint, reducing the search space logarithmically rather than linearly.
steps: Ensure the inventory list is maintained in a strictly sorted order.
Use bisect_left to identify the precise index where a new product ID belongs.
Verify the target index does not exceed the list bounds.
Perform the insertion or retrieval operation at the identified index.
outcome: Rapid identification of record positions, enabling high-frequency inventory management without full-list re-sorting.
limitation: The bisection algorithm is not thread-safe; concurrent mutations to the list during a search result in undefined behavior, requiring external synchronization.

diagram.title: Bisection Search Logic
diagram.description: The process of narrowing down the search space for a target value.

code.content:
import bisect
# Maintain sorted inventory IDs
inventory = [101, 105, 110, 120]
new_id = 108
# Find insertion point to keep list sorted
idx = bisect.bisect_left(inventory, new_id)
# Insert the new ID at the correct position
inventory.insert(idx, new_id)
code.explanation: This demonstrates using bisect_left to find the correct index for a new product ID, ensuring the list remains sorted for future binary searches.
